# Pumble MCP server for AI agents and assistants

Securely connect your AI agents and chatbots (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc) with Pumble MCP or direct API to send channel messages, manage direct messages, schedule announcements, and search workspace conversations through natural language.

![Pumble logo](https://logos.composio.dev/api/pumble)Pumble

Api Key

Pumble is a team communication platform for channels, direct messages, scheduled messages, and workspace collaboration. It helps teams keep conversations organized, searchable, and easy to act on.

9 Tools

Type what you want done — sign in and watch it run live in the Tool Router playground.

TOOLS

## Supported Tools

Every Pumble action and event your agent gets out of the box.

Delete Message

Permanently delete one Pumble message identified by channel ID and message ID.

Edit Message

Replace the text of an existing Pumble message in a channel.

Get Current User

Return the Pumble user and workspace associated with the connected API key.

Get Message

Fetch one Pumble message by its message ID and channel ID.

List Channel Messages

Return one page of recent messages from a channel, continuing backward through history with a cursor.

List Channels

List channels and direct-message conversations belonging to the connected Pumble user, including channel IDs needed by message tools.

List Users

List users in the current Pumble workspace with stable IDs and profile details.

Search Messages

Search Pumble messages and return one bounded page.

Send Message

Immediately post a text message to a Pumble channel identified by its channel ID.

SETUP GUIDE

## Connect Pumble MCP Tool with your Agent

1

#### Install Composio

typescript

```
npm install @composio/core ai @ai-sdk/mcp @ai-sdk/openai
```

Install the Composio SDK and your agent framework

2

#### Create a session with MCP enabled

typescript

```
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const { mcp } = await composio.create("your-user-id", {
  toolkits: ["pumble"],
  mcp: true,
});
```

Create a session scoped to Pumble and read its MCP URL and headers

3

#### Connect your agent to the MCP server

typescript

```
import { createMCPClient } from "@ai-sdk/mcp";
import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
import { generateText, stepCountIs } from "ai";

const client = await createMCPClient({
  transport: { type: "http", url: mcp.url, headers: mcp.headers },
});

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: openai("gpt-5.6-sol"),
  tools: await client.tools(),
  prompt: "Post a message to the #general channel in Pumble saying the daily standup starts in 10 minutes",
  stopWhen: stepCountIs(10),
});

console.log(text);
await client.close();
```

Pass the session's MCP URL and headers to your agent and run a Pumble request

SETUP GUIDE

## Connect Pumble API Tool with your Agent

1

#### Install Composio

typescript

```
npm install @composio/core @composio/openai openai
```

Install the Composio SDK, the OpenAI provider, and the OpenAI SDK

2

#### Create a Composio session

typescript

```
import OpenAI from "openai";
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";
import { OpenAIResponsesProvider } from "@composio/openai";

const composio = new Composio({ provider: new OpenAIResponsesProvider() });
const client = new OpenAI();

const session = await composio.create("your-user-id", { toolkits: ["pumble"] });
const tools = await session.tools();
```

Initialize Composio with the OpenAI Responses provider and create a session scoped to Pumble

3

#### Run Pumble tools with your agent

typescript

```
let response = await client.responses.create({
  model: "gpt-5.6-sol",
  tools,
  input: [{ role: "user", content: "Post a message to the #general channel in Pumble saying the daily standup starts in 10 minutes" }],
});

while (response.output.some((o) => o.type === "function_call")) {
  const outputs = await composio.provider.handleToolCalls(session, response.output);
  response = await client.responses.create({
    model: "gpt-5.6-sol",
    tools,
    previous_response_id: response.id,
    input: outputs,
  });
}

console.log(response.output_text);
```

Send a request, execute the Pumble tool calls through the session, and print the final answer

## Why Use Composio?

### AI Native Pumble Integration

- Supports both Pumble MCP and direct API based integrations
- Structured, LLM-friendly schemas for reliable tool execution
- Rich coverage for sending messages, reading conversations, and working across Pumble channels and direct messages

### Managed Auth

- Secure API key handling without hard-coding Pumble credentials in your agent code
- Central place to manage, scope, and revoke Pumble access
- Per user and per environment credentials so your dev, staging, and production agents stay cleanly separated

### Agent Optimized Design

- Tools are shaped so language models can understand Pumble actions like posting messages, checking channels, and finding conversations
- Tools are tuned using real error and success rates to improve reliability over time
- Comprehensive execution logs so you always know what ran, when, and on whose behalf

### Enterprise Grade Security

- Fine-grained RBAC so you control which agents and users can access Pumble
- Scoped, least privilege access to Pumble workspace resources
- Full audit trail of agent actions to support review and compliance

FAQ

## Frequently asked questions

###

###

Yes! Composio's Tool Router enables agents to use multiple toolkits. [Learn more](https://docs.composio.dev/tool-router/overview).

###

Yes. Composio is SOC 2 Type II compliant and is built to keep your Pumble connection and credentials secure. OAuth tokens and API keys are encrypted, and sensitive customer data is protected at rest and in transit.

Composio also undergoes independent security testing and continuously monitors its systems for security threats. You can review the latest reports and policies in the [Composio Trust Center](https://trust.composio.dev).

###

Composio maintains and updates all toolkit integrations automatically, so your agents always work with the latest API versions.

###

Create the key in your Pumble account settings, then paste it once on Composio's connection page. Composio stores it encrypted and uses it only for the Pumble actions your agent runs. Nobody else in your workspace can read it, and you can revoke it inside Pumble at any time.

###

When you connect a Pumble account through Composio, every action runs under that account, so anything the agent creates, sends, or changes shows up in Pumble as done by you. Keep an approval step in your prompt for actions with side effects, such as sending or deleting, and have the agent draft first.

###

Whatever the credentials you connect allow inside Pumble. If Pumble lets you scope a key to specific permissions, create a scoped one so the agent can only do what you intend. You can revoke the key inside Pumble at any time.

###

Yes. Composio supports multiple connected accounts for the same app, and that works in Claude, ChatGPT, or any other assistant you connect through Composio. Give each Pumble connection a name such as work or personal, and the assistant uses the one you mention in the request. Each account keeps its own credentials and nothing is merged.

###

The connection stops working the moment Pumble rejects the old key. Create a new key in Pumble and reconnect the account from the Composio dashboard or by asking your agent to reconnect Pumble. Nothing else changes.

###

Composio's free Hobby plan includes 100,000 tool calls per month with no credit card, which covers most personal Pumble use. Paid plans add higher limits and team features. Your Pumble plan and its API limits still apply as usual.

###

Built-in connectors usually give one AI access to a limited set of apps. Many people use Composio because it lets their AI connect to more apps than it normally supports, or connect to multiple accounts for the same app (e.g. connect Claude to multiple Pumble accounts).

With Composio, you connect Pumble once and then use it across different AI assistants without setting it up separately in each one. Connect your apps to Composio once, then connect Composio to whichever AI you use, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT, Hermes, or your own custom assistant.
